description: The US Environmental Protection Agency publishes a Python implementation of Intelligent Dasymetric Mapping using open-source GIS libraries. The command-line tool accepts population polygons, a categorical ancillary raster and optional uninhabited-area polygons. It estimates densities for land-cover classes and allocates polygon totals to cells, producing GeoTIFF rasters and CSV working tables. Geographic coverage, time reference and resolution follow the supplied inputs; a documented example uses Delaware census and land-cover data. GitHub supplies an environment file and Python 3.6 usage instructions under MIT, with free source access. The earlier archived release uses a generic other-open licence label. A limitation is that density assumptions and the choice of sampling thresholds affect local allocation, while the older software environment may require adjustment. The outputs can support flood-exposure or public-service demand simulations. This implementation complements the separate ArcGIS toolbox without requiring that proprietary GIS runtime. Dependencies were not installed.
